rationale: Author-of-record confirmation of the round-1 fix commit 44690044 (exactly ONE commit atop the round-1 SHA 2691189d, as required). Diff confinement verified: five files (internal/bead/{bdcli.go,bdcli_test.go}, internal/next/{beads.go,beads_test.go,ready_gate.go}), every hunk mapping to a consolidated gate item — G1 (bdRenderedError wrapper: Error() = renderBDError escaped text, Unwrap() = original error unchanged, embedded via %w at QueryReady/QueryReadyForEpic, beads.go:39/:55 — this restores the errors.As/Is chain my round-1 OBSERVATION and R5's RC flagged, the right design), G2 (same wrapper at FetchBeadByID beads.go:253, FetchBeadAsOf beads.go:278, and GateReadiness ready_gate.go:73 — R3's armed-leg RC), G4 (wrapBDError whitespace-only-stderr passthrough via TrimSpace BEFORE decoration, bdcli.go:488-490 — R5's RC). No unrelated rewrites: FetchBead* message prefixes unchanged; for printable diagnostics bdRenderedError.Error() is byte-identical to the underlying Error() (termsafe.Escape returns all-printable lines unchanged), so no downstream text consumer sees a change. Parallel-track confinement verified against bead 7's ACTUAL branch surface (git diff --name-only bed348c2 bead/mindspec-ta30.7): bead 7 touches cmd/mindspec/next.go, internal/next/guard.go, internal/next/entangle_test.go and others — ZERO overlap with the fix's five files; touching ready_gate.go was therefore safe (R3's overlap worry does not hold in fact), and the G3 deferral is correct precisely BECAUSE cmd/mindspec/next.go IS bead 7's active file. G3's deferral is properly recorded: rationale in the commit message (tracedCombined discard gap means the RecordReadinessOverride leg carries no folded stderr today; describePhaseSyncFailure legs need the treatment once next.go frees up) and follow-up bead mindspec-6gsy exists and is open — verified via bd. Double-escape through nested bdRenderedError layers (GateReadiness over an already-wrapped FetchBead error) is idempotent by construction since Escape output is printable. Chain-restoration is regression-pinned at every level R5 asked: wrapper unit (TestBdRenderedError_UnwrapExposesUnderlyingError), end-to-end errors.As through QueryReady (TestQueryReady_ErrorsAsReachesExitError), production-consumer classification through FetchBeadAsOf (TestFetchBeadAsOf_IsUnsupportedFlagErrorClassifiesThroughWrapper), BeadExists with non-empty stderr so the wrap path is actually exercised (TestBeadExists_NotFoundWithNonEmptyStderr), and G4's four whitespace shapes (TestWrapBDError_WhitespaceOnlyStderrPassesThrough). Verified firsthand in the bead worktree at 44690044 (clean, byte-identical): gofmt -l clean on both packages, go build ./... green, go test -short -count=1 green on internal/bead (5.8s) and internal/next (14.5s) including all new tests.

findings.title: R3's per-leg hostile-shim RENDERING test on a G2 leg delivered as classification-only; rendering safety on the new legs rests on the shared wrapper type + its unit pin
findings.detail: R3's round-1 RC asked for a hostile-shim regression test on at least one of the newly-escaped legs (fake bd failing on `show` with control-bearing stderr) asserting no raw control byte reaches the rendered output. The delivered TestFetchBeadAsOf_IsUnsupportedFlagErrorClassifiesThroughWrapper drives a real shim through FetchBeadAsOf but with printable stderr, asserting classification, not control-byte absence. The rendering property on the new legs IS pinned, but indirectly: all four legs embed the identical bdRenderedError type, whose Error()-escapes-control-bytes behavior is directly unit-tested (TestBdRenderedError_UnwrapExposesUnderlyingError) and end-to-end-tested on the QueryReady leg through the same %w-embedding construction (TestQueryReady_AC11RenderingLeg still passes through the wrapper). What is NOT pinned: a future revert of one specific leg (say FetchBeadByID) from &bdRenderedError{err: err} back to bare err would break no test. I judge this non-blocking under my lens — the property is structural and the revert is a plainly visible one-line diff — but R3 owns this ask; their round-2 re-verdict is the authority on whether the indirect pin satisfies it, and a one-test follow-up on the G3 bead (mindspec-6gsy) would close it cheaply if not.
